evidence.quoted_text: requested, input_scope, reviewed = map(scope, (p["requested_scope"], p["input_scope"], p["reviewed_scope"]))
evidence.reason: The validator builds all three scope maps at line 209 via map(scope, ...), and scope() expands every interval row by materializing each line into a set through intervals()/result.update(range(...)) at line 170. The visible code has only a per-file/interval cap and no aggregate decoded-entry cap before the subset checks, so a self-consistent record under the byte cap can contain many rows and scopes that expand to millions of Python set entries, causing memory amplification during validation. This is an implementation defect in the intended integrity checking, not merely an optional hardening request. The smallest compatible fix is to sum interval sizes across all rows and all three scopes before constructing any sets and reject records whose total expanded entries exceed a chosen bound that keeps valid reviews admissible.
